newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF bureau to shift focus to long-term JGBs - paper. [CORRECTED 06:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MOF bureau to shift focus to long-term JGBs - paper. [CORRECTED 06:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects throughout to read that bonds will be held for five years and longer, not have maturities of that period.)

The Japanese Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau will shift its investment focus to holding Japanese government bonds (JGBs) for five years and longer, the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun quoted government sources as saying on Wednesday.
Until recently the bureau only held JGBs for a period of up to five years, the newspaper said.
But in fiscal 1997/98 most of the bureau's 2.4 trillion yen worth of investment funds will be held for five years or longer, it added.
Nihon Keizai said that the bureau on Tuesday purchased 100 billion yen worth of 10-year JGBs with remaining maturities longer than five years and it intends to hold them until redemption.
